notes: The shape follows DEPTH2 A03: fading is a state (current, less current, dormant, reconnecting), read from dated history, never a number shown or stored. Only the thresholds between states are open.

The thresholds are relative to each pair: a relationship stops being current after three of the pair's usual gaps between meetings (at least 60 days); it goes dormant after four times that, or a third of how long they have known each other, whichever is longer (at least a year); kin take three times as long; a single meeting is treated as a 90-day rhythm. Sharing a home or a workplace is never absence.

A03 says no universal pace is established and allows labelled private-playtest calibration. These are that calibration, labelled in the code. This asks whether any better evidence exists, or whether they should be judged in a playtest.
question: Are the calibrated thresholds at which a relationship stops being current and goes dormant reasonable, and is there evidence to set them better, including for kin, for colleagues who no longer work together, and for childhood friends?
requestedBy: lamontae, 2026-09-22 22:38Z: 'make sure questions are being written down. i dont want depth to be invented'

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Gives the shape and says pace follows contact rhythm, duration and life stage, but sets no thresholds and says qualitative pace needs a private playtest.
Chooses the interim thresholds. They are not researched.

title: When a relationship should stop being current, and when it goes dormant
usableAnswer: Either confirmation that the relative thresholds are a reasonable starting point for a playtest, or better ones with their basis, per kind of relationship (friend, kin, former colleague, childhood friend). A list of situations a playtester should check is also useful.
whyItMatters: These thresholds decide when the game tells the player 'you were close once' instead of 'you are close'. They are calibration by DEPTH2's own allowance, and the owner has now asked that nothing of this kind be invented without the question being written down.
